questions.stem: In alpha decay, what happens to the mass number and atomic number of the parent nucleus?

options.text: Mass number decreases by 2, atomic number decreases by 4
Mass number decreases by 4, atomic number decreases by 2
Mass number increases by 4, atomic number increases by 2
Mass number stays the same, atomic number decreases by 2

questions.explanation: In alpha decay, an alpha particle (2 protons + 2 neutrons) is emitted from the nucleus. This means the mass number decreases by 4 (losing 4 nucleons) and the atomic number decreases by 2 (losing 2 protons). The element changes to one two places lower in the periodic table.

questions.stem: In beta-minus decay, a neutron in the nucleus changes into which of the following?

options.text: A proton and a gamma ray
A proton and an electron (plus an antineutrino)
An alpha particle and a neutron

questions.explanation: In beta-minus decay, a neutron in the nucleus transforms into a proton and an electron (the beta particle), plus an antineutrino. The electron is ejected at high speed. The atomic number increases by 1, but the mass number stays the same since the total number of nucleons is unchanged.
